Subject: MSA redlines - termination / auto-renew / notice windows

Hi Dev,

Attached are our procurement redlines to the MSA and Order Form. High level: BrightHealth needs a guaranteed 60-day termination notice window for any renewal, and we can't accept open-ended auto-renew beyond one optional 12-month renewal without an explicit exec approval. We also requested a unilateral termination for convenience right on our side (to align with internal vendor consolidation timelines) with a 90-day notice.

Key asks:
- Confirm whether Redwood can accept mutual termination-for-convenience (TFC) with an explicit 60-day notice and a capped transition assistance fee (if applicable).
- If mutual TFC is unacceptable, can Redwood offer a limited unilateral right for customers under $200k TCV?
- Align on auto-renew mechanics: we prefer an opt-in renewal rather than automatic renew unless both parties sign-off on renewal order form.

We'd like to get legal alignment this week so procurement can clear the order before our next board review on 11/12. Can you confirm who at Redwood will own the redline discussion and a target timeline for a response?

Attachments: BrightHealth_MSA_Redlines_Nov03.pdf (redline)

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager
BrightHealth

Subject: Re: MSA redlines - termination / auto-renew / notice windows

Thanks for the ping — reviewed BrightHealth's redline. Below are proposed positions and a redline-ready clause we can offer. I'm keeping commercial flexibility in mind but protecting Redwood's operational and forecasting needs.

Position summary (recommended):
- Mutual TFC with 60-day written notice. Redwood will not accept unilateral customer TFC without commercial concessions (e.g., pro-rated minimums or termination fee) except for pilot accounts <= $150k TCV.
- Auto-renew: Propose an auto-renew only if the Order Form explicitly includes an "Auto-Renew Election" checkbox signed by both parties. By default, Order Forms expire at term end and require a new signed Order Form to continue service.
- Notice windows: Accept 60-day notice for termination actions. For mid-term cancellations that trigger operational disruption (e.g., reserved Dedicated capacity with committed spend), propose a 90-day notice and pro-rated early termination fee limited to 3 months of committed fees.

Proposed redline text (to paste into their PDF):
"Termination for Convenience. Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party. For Order Forms that include Reserved or Dedicated capacity commitments, termination shall require ninety (90) days' prior written notice and Customer shall pay a termination fee equal to the lesser of (a) three (3) months of then-current committed fees under the affected Order Form or (b) the remaining committed fees for the remainder of the then-applicable committed period. Notwithstanding the foregoing, for pilot engagements with Total Contract Value not exceeding One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (USD $150,000), Customer may exercise a unilateral termination for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice without additional termination fees."

On auto-renew:
"Order Form Renewal. Order Forms shall expire at the conclusion of the Term unless the parties execute a renewal Order Form or the Order Form contains an explicit, signed Auto-Renew Election. Absent a signed Auto-Renew Election, services will not continue on an automatic basis and any continued service will require a new signed Order Form."

Next steps:
- Dev / Marissa: confirm commercial willingness on the pilot carveout threshold ($150k) and the early termination fee cap (3 months).
- If commercial agrees, I'll produce a tracked-change PDF to send to Samantha.
- If BrightHealth pushes for a unilateral broad TFC, we should ask for a revenue protection (minimums) or an onboarding cost reimbursement schedule.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call with Samantha & Tom tomorrow 9:00–9:30am PST to walk through live.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
